aboutH2: Red Road Ranch: Lodge and Cabin Addiction Treatment Near Lumby, BC
intro: Red Road Recovery is an addictions treatment centre for substance abuse and concurrent disorders located in Lumby BC. Our rehabilitation program focuses on healing the mind, body and spirit through the bio/pyscho-social model, integrated with traditional indigenous healing practices and recovery through the 12 Steps. We believe everyone is different with their own underlying issues and needs, hence why we believe in building individualized treatment plans structured to address each client specifically. We have three other locations currently: Red Road Recovery in Sorrento, Red Road Rise in Salmon Arm and Red Road North in Terrace BC.

The Ranch opened in early 2024 and is the largest Red Road house, with 25 beds spread between a log lodge and cabins on a 114-acre mountainside property in Creighton Valley. It is also the location where Red Road offers equine therapy.

pillars.title: A Working Valley Property Above Lumby
pillars.body: The Ranch sits in Creighton Valley, the road east of Lumby that climbs toward Echo Lake Provincial Park. Its 114 acres take in a main log lodge with a big dining room, a cluster of red-roofed cabins, open pasture and forest. A large round yurt with a circle of chairs is used for groups and gatherings. Residents sleep in the lodge or the cabins, and the centre's own photos show hikes to nearby waterfalls and lakes in summer and snowy walks in winter.

pillars.title: Horses, Ceremony and the 12 Steps
pillars.body: Days at the Ranch follow the Red Road program of group and one-on-one counselling, recovery education and an introduction to the 12 Steps. What sets this house apart is the land. Sheila Wardman works as both counsellor and equine lead, and David Villanueva runs cultural programming that can include smudging, medicine wheel teachings, sweat lodge and crafts such as pottery, rattles and medicine bags. The centre's photos also show residents out hiking on the surrounding land.

pillars.title: Counsellors Who Have Walked the Same Road
pillars.body: Operations Manager Richard Bellinger is a Canadian Certified Addiction Counsellor and Medication Assisted Treatment Specialist who works from a trauma-informed, attachment-aware approach. Steve Braun, a Registered Therapeutic Counsellor and Certified Recovery Coach with 18 years of sobriety, has been at the Ranch since it opened and also runs virtual one-to-one sessions before and after treatment. Counsellor Jesse Niall completes the clinical team, and like all Red Road staff they bring personal experience of recovery.

overview: Red Road Ranch is a CARF-accredited, co-ed residential program for adults 19 and over, run as a registered supportive recovery residence under Interior Health. Stays last 30, 45, 60 or 90 days. Counsellors write an individual plan with each resident, and the program combines evidence-based counselling, the 12 Steps and Indigenous cultural teachings offered with local community partners. The house is staffed 24/7 and in-house chefs cook the meals.

location.heading: Red Road Ranch in Lumby, British Columbia
location.intro: The Ranch is at 1129 Creighton Valley Road, in the hills east of the village of Lumby in the North Okanagan, about 15 to 20 minutes from town and roughly 40 minutes from Vernon. Vancouver is about 5.5 hours away by the Coquihalla and the Okanagan Connector, Kelowna about 1 hour 30 minutes and Kamloops about 2 hours.

faqIntro: Answers come from the centre's listing and its own website. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: What makes Red Road Ranch different from the other Red Road houses?
faqs.a: The Ranch is the biggest and most rural Red Road location, with 25 beds in a lodge and cabins on 114 acres near Lumby. It is the house that offers equine therapy, and its land is used for cultural activities and hikes. The core counselling program is the same across all locations.

faqs.q: How much does Red Road Ranch cost?
faqs.a: Red Road does not publish its prices; its website asks you to contact the centre. The Ranch has publicly funded beds that are free for eligible BC residents and private beds paid by the client, family, a First Nation Band, an employer or insurance. FNHA subsidy and Medicard payment plans are also available.

faqs.q: Are there free, publicly funded beds at the Ranch?
faqs.a: Yes. The centre says the Ranch has both privately and publicly funded beds. Funded beds come from a CMHA grant, are for BC residents aged 19 and over and need no income verification. Admissions on 250-800-3190 can tell you the current wait.

faqs.q: How long do people stay at Red Road Ranch?
faqs.a: Stays are 30, 45, 60 or 90 days, which Red Road calls its Intensive, Enhanced, Comprehensive and Extensive programs. The right length depends on your history, and admissions will go through the options with you.

faqs.q: Where is Red Road Ranch and how do I get there?
faqs.a: The Ranch is at 1129 Creighton Valley Road, east of Lumby in BC's North Okanagan. It is about 40 minutes from Vernon, 1 hour 30 minutes from Kelowna and about 5.5 hours from Vancouver. Kelowna International Airport is the nearest major airport.

faqs.q: Does Red Road Ranch offer detox?
faqs.a: No. You need to be detoxed or medically fit for treatment at intake, so plan withdrawal management with your doctor or health authority before you come. Admissions can help you work out timing.

faqs.q: Who can attend Red Road Ranch?
faqs.a: Adults aged 19 and over can attend, and the program is co-ed. Referrals can come from you, a First Nation Band, a health authority, a shelter or a counsellor. Applicants with sexual charges or offences are not accepted.

faqs.q: What support is there after I leave the Ranch?
faqs.a: Red Road offers aftercare that includes virtual one-to-one counselling and support meetings; counsellor Steve Braun provides virtual sessions and aftercare support for the network. recovery.com also lists online follow-up sessions, recovery retreats and alumni reunions.

Yes. Red Road Recovery has a three-year CARF accreditation that the centre says covers all programs and locations. The Ranch is also registered with BC's assisted living registry as a supportive recovery residence.
